findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can opener was observed with dry debris contaminating it. The PIC was shown and moved the item to dish for cleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a ready-for-use sanitizer (sani bucket) in the kitchen areas. When asked a bucket was produce at effective concentration for the kitchen that corrected the immediate violation. Ensure that a ready-for use sanitizer is available at all times that the facility is handling or preparing foods and food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

The CFPMs available for the facility had not completed the required allergen training at the time of the inspection. Education was conducted and the PIC was instructed to have the required training completed and the certificates available prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine in the bar area was tested at 0ppm. After several cycles, a bottle replacement, and priming of the machine, the concentration tested at 100ppm (CL). It appears that the chlorine bottle was empty and needed to be replaced. Additionally, the sanitizer chemical (at triple sink) in the kitchen area was also tested at 0ppm (CL). The facility uses the chemical at the dispenser to sanitize food contact surfaces. Instructed the facility to manually make the buckets until the dispenser can be serviced. Violation corrected on site. Ensure that sanitizer concentrations are always testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was a slight accumulation of dried debris on the food contact surfaces of the can opener. Shown to the owner and the can opener was placed through the dish machine to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There were several boxes of food stored on the floors of the walk in cooler and walk in freezer. Suggested purchasing metal racks (or crates) that are at least six inches from the floor to protect against contamination. Ensure that food is never stored on the floor and is at least six inches from ground level.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build-up of food debris behind the cook line. Discussed with PIC, and PIC stated that the kitchen is professionally cleaned once a month. Ancillary cleaning in-between professional cleanings may be required to keep this area clean. Ensure the cook-line equipment is cleaned behind regularly enough to keep the area clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Inspector observed an employee wash hands and use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet. He then use the same paper towel to dry hands. Employee was coached and properly washed hands. Train hand washing continually. Violation is considered corrected on site. 
(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Inspector observed the counter in the men’s restroom is no longer sealed to the par wall separating it from the urinal. Seal the counter to the wall. 
PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Ice scoop was observed in the bar ice bin with the handle in contact with the ice.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure ice scoops are stored with the hand out of the ice to prevent contamination.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of caulk:
-Kitchen hand sink
-Bar hand sink
Ensure these areas are sealed to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.
